scripts.radio:
Hamjambo listeners, this is Kenyans Are Asking, where we keep track of promises, public money, and power.

First, on youth and employment: over one hundred thousand comrades leave our universities every single year, stepping directly into an economy that demands experience but offers zero pay. Despite official pledges guaranteeing paid internships, thousands of graduates remain trapped in unpaid labor. Free work is not employment, and policy delivery must match political rhetoric.

Over at the Central Bank, however, a promise was delivered. The CBK has modernized government bond trading by launching a dealer-led platform, improving transparency and opening up local debt markets. It proves that when institutional focus is present, targets can be met.

Finally, amid renewed political chatter about extending the presidential term limit, let us be clear on the law. No politician and no Parliament can alter presidential term limits through a routine legislative vote. Under Article 255 of our Constitution, any amendment affecting the term of office of the President requires an approval by the people through a national referendum. The final say does not belong to politicians; it belongs to you.

Kwa ufupi: Zaidi ya wahitimu laki moja wanakabiliwa na kazi za bure licha ya ahadi za kulipwa. Benki Kuu imezindua mfumo mpya wa biashara ya bondi kama ilivyoahidi. Na kuhusu wanaopanga kuongeza muda wa urais, Katiba inasema wazi—hakuna mbunge anayeweza kubadilisha hilo bila kura ya maoni kutoka kwa wananchi wenyewe. Stay informed, stay vigilant.
scripts.voice_note:
Habari yenu, quick accountability update from Kenyans Are Asking this week.

First, do not be misled by political chatter about MPs extending presidential term limits. The Constitution is unequivocal: altering the presidential term cannot be done within Parliament alone. Under Article 255, it mandates a direct national referendum. The ultimate decision rests with the Kenyan voter, not legislators in Nairobi.

On the job market, over one hundred thousand comrades graduate annually into unpaid internships, despite high-level commitments to deliver paid placements. Real talent cannot run on empty promises.

On the flip side, Central Bank has kept its word, modernizing bond trading through a dealer-led market to make public borrowing more transparent.

Head over to our Glasspoll today and vote on whether presidential terms should stay at five years or change. Let us know what you think.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: MPs cannot quietly extend presidential terms. Article 255 requires a mandatory national referendum. Your vote alone decides constitutional changes.
scripts.reels: Can Parliament quietly change the presidential term limit? The short answer is no. Whatever political trial balloons are floated, Article 255 of the Constitution settles the matter. No bill, no coalition, and no majority in Parliament can alter the term of office of the President on their own. It legally mandates a national referendum. The power belongs to you at the ballot, not politicians in boardroom deals.
